port_difficulty.why: Three executable statements: ACCEPT a name, CALL it, STOP RUN. No arithmetic and no files. The one hard part is that the target is a run-time string, so the target platform needs an explicit dispatch table or a dynamic loader.

blast_radius.why: It can start any program whose name arrives on the input card, including programs outside this tree. The CALL has no ON EXCEPTION clause, so a bad name abends the job. The tree holds no JCL or scheduler entry, so I cannot tie it to the nightly batch cycle. That is a gap, not evidence that it is safe.

units.driving_fact: PROGA calls a program named by a value it ACCEPTs at run time, so the callee set cannot be read from the source.

port_difficulty.why: One statement, GOBACK. Nothing to translate.

blast_radius.why: It does nothing, so a wrong port is loud only if it fails to load. Its real exposure is that PROGA may call it by name, which the source cannot confirm. It is the only in-tree program PROGA could reach.

units.driving_fact: PROGB has no static caller and is a possible target of PROGA's computed call.
